channel.title: Acme: Tech News
channel.description: Articles about software, publishing and the open web.

item.title: WordPress 7.1.4 closes upgrade-window and stored-XSS vulnerabilities
item.description: WordPress 7.1.4 is a security release addressing an upgrade-process weakness that could permit remote code execution during an update window, plus stored cross-site scripting, denial-of-service and privacy flaws. Fixes were backported through WordPress 4.7, and site owners are urged to update promptly.

item.title: PodcastOne explores a sale after receiving buyer interest
item.description: PodcastOne has formed a special committee and hired a financial adviser to consider a sale after receiving interest from multiple potential buyers. The podcast network's shares jumped on the announcement, though they remained below their May level. The process could also lead to another strategic transaction or no deal.

item.title: What $20 million in flexible grants changed for 205 local newsrooms
item.description: Press Forward distributed $20 million to 205 small local newsrooms, usually as $100,000 in unrestricted support over two years. Nieman Lab found the money helped recipients plug budget holes, test products and stabilize operations, but the short grant period often was not enough to sustain permanent hiring.

item.title: Beehiiv is turning solo newsletters into small newsrooms
item.description: CJR talks with Beehiiv’s Preeya Goenka about a media collective that waives platform fees and provides legal, healthcare and audience support for two years. The program still serves solo writers, but some members now operate multi-reporter local and national newsrooms.

item.title: Only 32% express high confidence in accurate midterm results coverage
item.description: A nationally representative Medill and Alliance for Trust in Media survey found six in ten Americans have at least some confidence in election reporting, but only 32% have quite a bit or a great deal. Distrust is sharply polarized by party.

item.title: A politics podcast plans live midterm coverage across video and RSS
item.description: Goalhanger’s The Rest Is Politics: US will stream a three-hour election-results special with Katty Kay and Anthony Scaramucci, plus five advance livestreams. Recordings will also flow into the show’s podcast feed, joining live video with open audio distribution.

item.title: Dave Winer resumes work on rss.chat after modernizing Frontier
item.description: Winer says he has returned to rss.chat after converting Frontier to run on modern operating systems and building a new application. The short update captures the practical challenge of re-entering a fast-moving personal codebase after only a few months away.

item.title: Dial Flipper uses open RSS to make podcast discovery feel like radio
item.description: Podnews reports that the new iOS app drops listeners into the middle of unfamiliar shows with a turn of a virtual dial, then learns from their choices. Because playback uses open RSS, each listen is still counted by the publisher's podcast host.

item.title: India offers talks after publishers challenge its privacy law
item.description: India's technology minister invited editors to submit concerns and said the government could act to protect press freedom. The statement is the first official response since 21 publishers argued the law could expose sources and force consent from investigation subjects.

item.title: Egyptian court orders leading independent news site closed
item.description: A court convicted Mada Masr editor Lina Attalah of operating without a license, fined the outlet and ordered its site closed and equipment confiscated. Press-freedom groups call the case an unprecedented attack on one of Egypt's few prominent independent newsrooms.

item.title: Podcast 2.0 metadata and Podping make open audio more useful in real time
item.description: A developer guide shows how standard RSS tags expose transcripts, chapters, people and soundbites while Podping announces feed changes within minutes. Together they support searchable episodes, guest pages and timely indexes without surrendering distribution to one platform.

item.title: WordPress 7.2 Beta 2 advances editor and developer APIs
item.description: The second beta refines WordPress administration, content querying, schema handling and permissions while expanding server-side registration for DataViews and DataForm. The project asks testers to use non-production sites ahead of the planned December 8 release.

item.title: Indian publishers challenge privacy law as a threat to investigative reporting
item.description: Reuters reports that 21 publishers asked India’s Supreme Court to strike provisions that could require consent from investigation subjects, compel deletion of published reports and expose confidential sources. The case is a major test of privacy rules against press freedom.

item.title: TPAC puts practical web standards and browser interoperability on the table
item.description: W3C’s 2026 breakout agenda spans semantic HTML, accessibility testing, browser extensions, client-side includes, privacy and the organizations that shape standards. The public session descriptions show how open-web proposals move from developer needs toward interoperable specifications.

item.title: WordPress portability helps restore a 6,500-post journalism archive
item.description: When a Basque broadcaster shut down its blog network, journalist Roge Blasco’s 18-year travel archive disappeared. Because the original site used WordPress, its 6,500 posts could be exported, restored with audio and photos, and relaunched on an independent address.
